# Maven

Four `pom.xml` files, all in `Information-Systems-Modelling` — labs 2, 3, 4 and 5. The only Java
build tool in the source set; there is no Gradle anywhere. Labs 2–4 ship the **Maven wrapper**
(`mvnw` 3.3.2, resolving Maven 3.9.10); **lab 5 does not**, and `lab3/README.md` tells the reader to
run bare `mvn clean compile` regardless.

⚠ The root README's toolbelt table says "**Maven 3.9+** | labs 2–5 | or use the bundled wrapper
`mvnw`". Lab 5 has no wrapper, so the promise fails on a quarter of its own scope —
[[documentation-drift]].

## The one interesting plugin chain

Labs 2–4 do not hand-write their API interfaces. Three plugins cooperate:

1. **`openapi-generator-maven-plugin` 7.20.0** reads
   `src/main/resources/openapi/openapi.yaml` and generates Spring interfaces with
   `interfaceOnly=true` + `delegatePattern`, emitting into `target/generated-sources/openapi`.
2. **`build-helper-maven-plugin`** adds that directory to the compile source roots so javac sees it.
   *(Present in labs 3 and 4; lab 2 wires the generator without it.)*
3. **`spring-boot-maven-plugin`** packages the result.

This is the machinery behind [[contract-first-api-design]], and it has a second-order consequence
worth noting: because the controllers implement *generated* interfaces, hand-adding cross-cutting
code to them is fragile — which is the stated reason lab 4 reaches for
[[aspect-oriented-programming]] instead.

The generated tree is also why a naive file count over this repo reports **231 Java files** when the
tracked source is **134**: `target/` holds build copies of everything.

## Dependency management, not just dependencies

- Labs 2–4 inherit from `spring-boot-starter-parent`, so Spring, Jackson and JPA versions come from
  the BOM rather than from pins. See [[spring-boot]].
- Lab 5 inherits from nothing and imports **`rdf4j-bom`** in `dependencyManagement` for the same
  effect on the RDF4J side. See [[rdf4j]].
- Only the genuinely external things are pinned by hand: `sqlite-jdbc` 3.49.1.0 and
  `hibernate-community-dialects` (lab 2), `h2` (labs 3–4), jjwt 0.12.6 (lab 4),
  springdoc 2.8.9 / 2.8.13, `jakarta.xml.bind-api` 4.0.0.
- Lab 5 uses **`exec-maven-plugin` 3.1.0** as its run mechanism — no Spring Boot plugin, so
  `mvn exec:java` is the entry point.

## What Maven is *not* used for here

No `maven-surefire` configuration beyond the default, no failsafe, no jacoco, no checkstyle, no
shade/assembly, no release plugin, no CI that invokes any of it. The build produces jars and nothing
else; the verification story is thin and lives outside JUnit — see [[information-systems-modelling]].

Three of the seven labs use **no build tool at all**: labs 6 and 7 and the exam trainer are plain
Node with `dependencies: {}`. Lab 7's README says so in as many words, which is why
[[zero-dependency-no-build-step]] and Maven coexist in one repository without contradiction — they
cover disjoint halves of it.
